primitives.name: Referee Whistle Sound Detection
primitives.verbatim_quote: The proposed method is based on preprocessor, linear phase bandpass finite impulse response (FIR) filter shorttime energy estimator and decision logic.
primitives.assumptions: Audio signals are stationary within non-overlapping blocks; whistle sounds are distinct from ambient noise.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when background noise exceeds whistle amplitude or whistle frequency falls outside filter passband.

layer2.mapping: Maps audio energy peaks to temporal instants of whistle sounds via threshold-based decision logic in GSE's temporal state engine.
layer2.telemetry: Detection accuracy metrics (sensitivity, reliability) and false positive/negative counts.

primitives.name: Short-Time Energy Estimation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Then, the filtered signal is fed to short-time energy (STE) estimator which includes amplitude squarer and linear filter to obtain a positive signal.
primitives.assumptions: Signal energy variations over short windows capture transient whistle characteristics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Performance degrades with insufficient window size leading to ripple artifacts or excessive smoothing.

layer2.mapping: STE output mirrors temporal structure of whistle presence in GSI's probabilistic model space.
layer2.telemetry: Local maxima in STE signal used to identify potential whistle onset/offset times.

primitives.name: Decision Logic Thresholding
primitives.verbatim_quote: In this work, we use decision rules based on the amplitude-dependent threshold and time-dependent threshold for detecting of referee whistle sound regions.
primitives.assumptions: Whistle sound amplitude exceeds baseline noise floor; temporal consistency confirms valid whistle occurrence.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Threshold misalignment leads to false positives or missed detections due to variability in whistle intensity or timing.

layer2.mapping: Threshold comparisons in GSE trigger highlight extraction logic upon confirmed whistle instants.
layer2.telemetry: Number of detected whistle instances and associated FP/FN rates.

The filtered signal undergoes short-time energy estimation through amplitude squaring and smoothing filters, producing a feature signal that highlights transient energy bursts. Decision logic applies both amplitude-dependent and time-dependent thresholds to localize whistle sound instants. This process enables precise timestamping of whistle events, which are then used to segment video content into highlights. The system's robustness depends on accurate threshold selection and filter design to minimize false positives and negatives. Sensitivity of 92.5% and reliability of 80.5% indicate strong performance despite 19.4% failure rate involving 42 false positives and 26 false negatives across 12+ hours of audio data.
